text:
alex: heads-up: i've been experimenting with a 'micro-credit' approach for prefix eviction instead of immediate hard demotes. wanted to get quick feedback.
mina: whats the core idea?
alex: callers can hand small "reclaim credits" to shards for a prefix. shards spend credits to run bounded slab scans/demote passes. credits expire; if memory still high, sequencer can hard-evict.
raj: so credits act like prepaid work tokens. does this change read visibility or leases?
alex: no. visibility/leases unaffected. credits only bias eviction order and give us smoother reclaim without big memory spikes.
mina: api sketch?
alex: POST /cache/reclaim_credit { "prefix": "acct:77/pfx:9", "units": "20", "ttl_ms": "3000", "req_id": "r-1845" }
raj: how do we avoid noisy-tenant abuse?
alex: same tenant quota checks, plus per-router credit-rate bucket. routers sign tokens for private installs.
mina: metrics we should add?
alex: credit_received, credit_consumed, bytes_reclaimed_per_unit, credits_expired, hard_evictions_after_credit. plus hist for credit->reclaim latency.
raj: rollout plan? small canary, compare hard-evict counts and tail latency. abort if hard-evicts increase or stale-read regressions.
ops-bot: infra-check: new endpoint minimal. needs two new metrics and a router ratelimit. no infra blockers.
mina: sounds reasonable. can you draft a short RFC follow-up with invariants and a tiny canary plan? i'll own the runbook.
alex: will do, pinging owners list and scheduling a 30m sync.
raj: thx — excited to see perf numbers.
